issue_title: PKA ECC DoubleBaseLadder RAM offsets overlap inputs/outputs -> invalid secp256r1 point on STM32H7S3L8
NUCLEO-H7S3L8 - Reference to nonexistent header in USB device example projects
clean_text:
Title: NUCLEO-H7S3L8 - Reference to nonexistent header in USB device example projects

Body:
Many of the projects in Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device have READMEs referring to "Header JP4"

This header does not exist whatsoever on the board, it is not anywhere in the schematics (MB1737 NUCLEO-H7S3L8) or the User Manual UM3276.

CDC_Standalone
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90264872-1e10-4084-9a53-1562a31e2990)

Composite_CDC_HID_Standalone
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/Composite_CDC_HID_Standalone

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0af09b4e-6776-437b-8432-25a3a28f81f9)

HID_Standalone
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/HID_Standalone

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e08612f-0541-427d-b49f-4b176dcf9b8f)

Video_Standalone
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/Video_Standalone

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49319019-d7e9-4205-85c2-d54111fd95de)

What header on the NUCLEO-H7S3L8 is this actually referring to? Potentially the UCPD option on power selector JP3?

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2025-04-23T14:45:34Z]
Hi @b4shful,

Thank you for the heads-up. Indeed, looks like a typo as there is no mention of any JP4 in the board's [manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um3276-stm32h7rx7sx-nucleo144-board-mb1737-stmicroelectronics.pdf). I'll let our development teams know about this in order to correct the typo.

With regards,

[ALABSTM - 2025-04-23T14:57:51Z]
ST Internal Reference: 208397

[ALABSTM - 2025-05-30T10:21:10Z]
Hi @b4shful,

I hope you are fine. It has been confirmed that the mention of JP4 should be replaced by JP3, as you guessed. We'll try to have these README.md files corrected.

With regards,

[ALABSTM - 2025-09-22T10:38:48Z]
Hi @b4shful,

Just to let you know that, eventually, it has been decided to **completely remove** the whole sentence It is mandatory ... JP4 from the the README files.

With regards,

[ALABSTM - 2025-09-30T14:47:46Z]
Fixed in commit 44ce964d296ac15779a4698131d9591da7a6978f

issue_title: LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw Triggers MPU HardFault on NUCLEO-H7S3L8
clean_text:
Title: LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw Triggers MPU HardFault on NUCLEO-H7S3L8

Body:
Hello,

I am working with a [NUCLEO-H7S3L8](https://www.st.com/en/evaluation-tools/nucleo-h7s3l8.html) (STM32-H7S3L8H6U).

When debugging the Application located at [Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw) , the MPU appears to trigger a HardFault Handler during LWIP initialization.

Stack Trace:

> Thread #1 [main] 1 [core: 1] (Suspended : Signal : SIGTRAP:Trace/breakpoint trap)	
> 	HardFault_Handler() at stm32h7rsxx_it.c:85 0x70001874	
> 	<signal handler called>() at 0xffffffe9	
> 	ptr_to_mem() at mem.c:452 0x7000bfb4	
> 	mem_init() at mem.c:531 0x7000c16e	
> 	lwip_init() at init.c:349 0x7000ac22	
> 	MX_LWIP_Init() at lwip.c:281 0x7000128e	
> 	main() at main.c:125 0x70001470	
> 	Reset_Handler() at startup_stm32h7s3l8hx.s:97 0x700006e6	

[IMAGE ATTACHED]

This application is set up to run as described in the Application's [README](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/blob/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw/README.md) where the XIP_Boot is loaded prior to the Appli in the Debug Configuration
[IMAGE ATTACHED]


The HardFault occurs when LWIP is attempting to calculate/access the end of the LWIP_RAM_HEAP at address 0x2404_3800.
[IMAGE ATTACHED]

I've checked the MPU configuration in the [project's IOC file](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/blob/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw.ioc), and it appears to cover the correct range, starting at address 0x2404_0000 and extending 16KB (well past 0x2404_3800)
[IMAGE ATTACHED]

This address space appears to be located within AXI SRAM3. Perhaps I am missing a configuration to enable the AXI bus?
[IMAGE ATTACHED]


If there is a configuration fix that I am missing, I am all ears. Much appreciated!

Comments:
[rneureuther1 - 2024-10-27T20:29:17Z]
I've found a solution by manually modifying the DTCM_AXI_SHARE Option Byte in CubeProgrammer. The hard fault no longer occurs. I'm unsure if the board shipped with this Option Byte set to 2, or if I changed it during experimentation myself.

- DTCM_AXI_SHARE should be set to 0 or 3 to set a DTCM value of 64KB. 
My value was originally set to 2, implying an extended DTCM size from 64KB to 192 KB. I believe this allowed the DTCM to extend into SRAM3, preventing the read/write to the SRAM3 region, resulting in a failure when allocation the LWIP_RAM_HEAP. 
[IMAGE ATTACHED]




Inspecting the Block Diagram showed that SRAM3 can be "shared DTCM". 
[IMAGE ATTACHED]


On page 159 of this document (https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0477-stm32h7rx7sx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) it I found this option byte described.
[IMAGE ATTACHED]

Adding this option byte to the [README's User Option Bytes requirement](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/blob/ea9d5c08521dc1918ac804b6079e8530f0746f49/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw/README.md?plain=1#L64C5-L64C34) may be beneficial for other developers

[ASEHSTM - 2024-11-07T10:32:29Z]
Hello @rneureuther1,
Thank you for your proposal. However, since the information is well-expressed in the reference manual, there is no need to add it to the README's user option bytes requirement. Therefore, please allow me to close this issue.

Thank you for your understanding.
With Regards,

issue_title: Adresses of SAI1 and SAI2 in CMSIS file is swapped
clean_text:
Title: Adresses of SAI1 and SAI2 in CMSIS file is swapped

Body:
Hi, I have a NUCLEO-H7S3L8 and I think there is an addresses mistake in the .svd files and potentially other hardware description files.

You can reproduce and see the mistake if you setup the SAI1_A and SAI1_B on CubeMX, generate the code and debug the program, you will see in the SFR widget of STM32CubeIDE (the .svd file) that it's the SAI2 registers configured instead.

It also affects the CubeMX configuration of SAI, we can't set SAI1_A on Master and SAI1_B on Slave synchronous which is very annoying (image below)

I'm not sure if it's the right place to report this, but I would really appreciate if you follow this issue on the right ST team.

Thanks.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e368e73-903f-49b3-b66e-c7cc58aabfde)

Comments:
[KRASTM - 2024-07-22T13:13:10Z]
ST Internal Reference: 189421

[KRASTM - 2024-08-26T13:55:11Z]
Hello @Protoxy22,

It appears that the issue is related to the CMSIS File not .svd file.

With regards.

[Protoxy22 - 2024-08-26T14:00:21Z]
> Hello @Protoxy22,
> 
> It appears that the issue is related to the CMSIS File not .svd file.
> 
> With regards.

Hi, ok I'm glad you have made progress on this

Thanks

[KRASTM - 2025-01-08T09:41:40Z]
Hello @Protoxy22,

I hope you're doing well. 

After further investigation, we found out that the mistake was indeed on **svd** file and the [RM0477](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0477-stm32h7rx7sx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf), section 2.3.2 Memory map and register boundary addresses. 
The RM has been recently updated. The fix for the SVD file, it will be available in the next release of CUBEIDE and other IDEs.

Thank you again, please allow me to close the issue.

With regards,

issue_title: USBD MSC does not support more than 2 luns
clean_text:
Title: USBD MSC does not support more than 2 luns

Body:
Hello,

In the function MSC_BOT_CBW_Decode() of the file usbd_msc_bot.c, there is the following judgment:

C
  if ((USBD_LL_GetRxDataSize(pdev, MSCOutEpAdd) != USBD_BOT_CBW_LENGTH) ||
      (hmsc->cbw.dSignature != USBD_BOT_CBW_SIGNATURE) ||
      (hmsc->cbw.bLUN > 1U) || (hmsc->cbw.bCBLength < 1U) ||
      (hmsc->cbw.bCBLength > 16U))
  {
    SCSI_SenseCode(pdev, hmsc->cbw.bLUN, ILLEGAL_REQUEST, INVALID_CDB);

    hmsc->bot_status = USBD_BOT_STATUS_ERROR;
    MSC_BOT_Abort(pdev);
  }
  else
  {
    /* ... */
  }


As shown in the above code, when **(hmsc->cbw.bLUN > 1U)** is established, it will be judged as an illegal request. Therefore, the legal value of **hmsc->cbw.bLUN** can only be 0 or 1. For this reason, USBD MSC can only support a maximum of 2 luns.

Why not add a MSC configuration macro definition in the file usbd_conf_template.h to configure the maximum number of luns supported?

Comments:
[ALABSTM - 2024-07-08T11:34:37Z]
See also [STM32CubeL4#41](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeL4/pull/41)

[ALABSTM - 2024-07-08T11:39:59Z]
ST Internal Reference: 126925

[ALABSTM - 2024-07-15T08:57:17Z]
Hi @xu-yingjing,

Our development teams acknowledged your request and agreed with the principle. However, there is currently no plan to address it. I will keep you informed should there be any news.

The request has been already logged internally. It will be tracked on GitHub via [this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeL4/pull/41) issue (mentioned above). Please allow me to close this one. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

Hi @AndrewCapon,

I noticed the error message is fatal error: stm32h7rsxx_hal.h: No such file or directory. This is due to the fact that the stm32h7rsxx_hal.h has not been found within your locally cloned copy of this repository. This is most likely due to the fact that the **submodules** needed by this repository have not been fetched.

As indicated in [this](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-use) section of the README.md file, you should use the --recursive when issuing the git clone command. This should resolve the issue.

There should be no problem with the template file you pointed out. Please allow me to close this thread. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

Title: No stm32cubeide project for the STM32H7S78-DK BSP project.

Body:
Hi Guys,

There is only EWARM available in https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/STM32H7S78-DK/Examples/BSP.

Is there a way of importing this into stm32cubeide?

Many thanks

Andy
